hero.lede: Every app on your iPhone is talking behind your back. Your location, your interests, where you spend your evenings. Privacy Score listens in. Locally. No server. No account.

hero.h1: Privacy Score: your iPhone App Privacy Report audit, fully on-device.

story.intro: No leak. No hack. Just a file purchased from a data broker, like anyone else can. The whole story in eight panels.

panels.caption: The Secret Service protects the President, around the clock, in silence. That's the job.

panels.captionStrong: Reporters buy a commercial ad dataset.
panels.caption: A hundred million location pings, for less than the price of a dinner. Perfectly legal.
Coming and going, day after day, around the White House.
Cross-referenced with a few public records. Not a hack. Legal. That's the problem.
A fitness app's global heatmap exposed the patrol routes of U.S. military personnel deployed overseas. For the whole world to see.
Hundreds of trackers a week on a single phone. Your location shipped to dozens of countries. Without you ever knowing.
Reads Apple's own report. Calculates a score out of 100. Tells you exactly what to fix. All on-device.
One score. Three fixes. The next data leak? It won't be yours.

pivot.line1Post: the data that's already out there.

product.body: Privacy Score reads the App Privacy Report that iOS is already generating on your iPhone. It cross-references every domain your apps contact with the open DuckDuckGo Tracker Radar database, then calculates a score, and tells you exactly what to fix.
bullets: Reads Apple's native report (no extra permissions).
Calculates the score on-device, in 2 seconds.
Surfaces 3 to 5 fixes you can apply right now.
Tracks your progress week after week.
product.phoneAlt: Privacy Score: privacy score of 67 out of 100 in context

steps.title: Export your report
steps.body: iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → App Privacy Report. You already have it: iOS records it quietly in the background.

steps.title: Privacy Score analyzes it
steps.body: Everything stays on your iPhone. We cross-reference the domains against DuckDuckGo's open database and compute a score out of 100.

steps.title: You fix. You watch the curve climb.
steps.body: Every recommendation tells you how many points it earns back. You apply the ones you want. You measure the progress.

manifesto.body: A privacy app has to be above reproach. The iOS source code is public. Here, line by line, is what we refuse to do.

cards.title: No server
cards.body: No in-house API. No analytics. Zero outbound requests.

cards.title: No account
cards.body: No sign-up. No email. No password.

cards.title: No cloud
cards.body: Your report lives in the iOS sandbox. Nowhere else.

cards.title: No panic
cards.body: No red badge. No urgent alerts. No “47 threats detected!” theatrics.

quote.body: Privacy Guard never sees your traffic. It shows you what everyone else sees of it.

items.q: Does Privacy Score see my browsing history?
items.a: No. Privacy Score only reads the App Privacy Report that iOS generates itself (Apple documentation): the list of apps that accessed your sensors and the domains they contacted. Your Safari history, your messages, your photos: never touched.

items.q: So how do you make money?
items.a: The app is free to download and free to use for your first complete scan, which stays accessible on your iPhone for life. To import a new report, you subscribe through Apple: €23.88 per year or €20.94 per six months. That is our only source of revenue. No advertising, no data resale, no partner pays us a commission.
Not yet. Privacy Score relies on the native iOS report, a feature Apple opened up in 2021. An Android version would depend on Google offering an equivalent.

items.q: What happens if I uninstall the app?
items.a: Everything goes. The report, the score history, your preferences: it all lives inside the iOS sandbox. Apple wipes it on uninstall. No copy anywhere else.

The iOS source code is public on GitHub and open to audit. The promises “no server, no account, fully on-device” are verifiable: search the codebase for  URLSession  and you'll find zero active calls.

cta.title: Take back control of your data.
cta.body: Sixty seconds to import your report. One score. Three fixes. And the quiet satisfaction of knowing exactly where you were leaking. And where you no longer are.
